_comment: PlenumNET TDNS — Canonical 81 (dimension × trit) meaning sentences. Version 1.0. Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Capomastro Holdings Ltd. DO NOT hardcode these in HTML or JSX — load at runtime.

1.label: Personal
1.meaning: Individual person or personal project — single operator, minimal accountability surface.

2.label: Corporate
2.meaning: Commercial or business entity operating for profit — registered company or startup.

3.label: Governance
3.meaning: Government body, public institution, or educational establishment — highest accountability standard.

1.label: Just me
1.meaning: Restricted to a single person or device — private by design, not listed publicly.

2.label: My group
2.meaning: Shared within a closed group, organisation, or team — not publicly accessible.

3.label: Everyone
3.meaning: Open to the public internet — reachable by any person with the URL.

1.label: Anonymous
1.meaning: Operator identity is anonymous or undisclosed — no verifiable accountability trail.

2.label: Known
2.meaning: Operator is identifiable but limited public disclosure — company name known, details sparse.

3.label: Transparent
3.meaning: Fully transparent — legal entity, contact information, and physical address publicly stated.

1.label: Self-hosted
1.meaning: Running on own hardware or privately managed infrastructure — full control, full responsibility.

2.label: Provider
2.meaning: Hosted by a third-party provider — shared or dedicated infrastructure with delegated operations.

3.label: Cloud
3.meaning: Cloud-native — running on a major public cloud or global edge network with SLA-backed availability.

1.label: Website
1.meaning: Static or server-rendered website — HTML/CSS content delivery, browser-first experience.

2.label: App / API
2.meaning: Dynamic application or API — server-side logic, programmable endpoints, or data exchange surface.

3.label: Device
3.meaning: Embedded or IoT endpoint — firmware service, hardware interface, or device-level protocol.

1.label: Text / HTML
1.meaning: Text-based content — HTML documents, structured data responses, or markdown rendering.

2.label: Media
2.meaning: Rich media — images, video, or audio served as the primary content format.

3.label: Live stream
3.meaning: Real-time continuous data emission — live video, audio stream, or persistent data feed.

1.label: Humans
1.meaning: Designed for human users — browser-rendered HTML, navigation-first interface.

2.label: Machines
2.meaning: Designed for machine consumers — JSON/XML API responses, structured data, no visual UI.

3.label: Both
3.meaning: Hybrid surface — serves both humans via UI and machines via API from the same origin.

1.label: No
1.meaning: No AI or machine learning signals detected — deterministic software logic only.

2.label: Partially
2.meaning: Partial AI presence — recommendation engine, ranking algorithm, or inference endpoint detected.

3.label: Yes
3.meaning: Full AI integration confirmed — model serving, LLM, or autonomous inference system active.

1.label: Private
1.meaning: Access is restricted or blocked — returns error, requires VPN, or is private network only.

2.label: Group
2.meaning: Partially accessible — requires authentication or returns partial content to anonymous requests.

3.label: Public
3.meaning: Fully public — accessible to any internet-connected client without credentials.

1.label: None
1.meaning: No authentication required — content is open to anonymous access with no login gate.

2.label: Password
2.meaning: Password-based authentication — standard login form, HTTP Basic, or API key required.

3.label: Strong ID
3.meaning: Strong identity verification — MFA, OAuth, certificate, or government identity check required.

1.label: Single server
1.meaning: Single server or minimal infrastructure — no redundancy, single point of failure present.

2.label: Several
2.meaning: Multiple servers or regional distribution — some redundancy, partial geographic coverage.

3.label: CDN / Many
3.meaning: CDN or global edge network — highly distributed delivery, anycast routing, DDoS mitigation.

1.label: HTTP
1.meaning: Standard HTTP/HTTPS — stateless request/response, the baseline web transport.

2.label: WebSocket
2.meaning: WebSocket — persistent bidirectional connection, real-time messaging capability established.

3.label: Raw TCP
3.meaning: Raw TCP or custom binary protocol — transport-layer service beyond HTTP.

1.label: Pre-2010
1.meaning: Pre-2010 technology stack — legacy headers, no modern browser security features, HTTP/1.1 only.

2.label: 2010s
2.meaning: 2010s technology stack — some modern headers present, partial security feature adoption.

3.label: 2020s+
3.meaning: 2020s+ technology stack — full modern header suite, HTTP/3, NEL, Reporting API, COOP/COEP.

1.label: Business hours
1.meaning: Business-hours availability — maintenance windows or limited uptime signals detected.

2.label: Extended
2.meaning: Extended availability — operational beyond business hours but not confirmed continuous.

3.meaning: 24/7 continuous operation — high uptime claims, no maintenance indicators, always-on signals.

1.label: Historical
1.meaning: Historical or cached data — content is static, infrequently updated, or long-TTL cached.

2.label: Current
2.meaning: Current data — regularly refreshed, moderate cache TTL, periodically updated content.

3.label: Live
3.meaning: Live data — real-time feed with zero cache, WebSocket or SSE delivery confirmed.

1.label: Batch
1.meaning: Batch processing — scheduled updates, high cache-control TTL, no streaming detected.

2.label: Near-real-time
2.meaning: Near-real-time — low cache TTL or short polling interval, sub-minute update cadence.

3.label: Real-time
3.meaning: Real-time — WebSocket, SSE, or gRPC streaming active, sub-second event delivery.

1.label: None
1.meaning: No financial transaction signals — informational or content-only service.

2.label: Accepts payment
2.meaning: Accepts payment — e-commerce checkout, payment gateway, or donation processing detected.

3.label: Processes
3.meaning: Processes financial transactions — wire transfers, ACH, or securities trading infrastructure.

1.label: Minimal
1.meaning: Minimal data collection — no tracking scripts, no form capture, no collection signals detected.

2.label: Moderate
2.meaning: Moderate data collection — standard analytics and form inputs present, limited third-party signals.

3.label: Heavy
3.meaning: Heavy data collection — multiple tracker categories and extensive form capture detected.

1.label: None
1.meaning: No legal or policy pages detected — no privacy policy, terms of service, or cookie notice.

2.label: Basic
2.meaning: Basic policies present — privacy policy or terms exist but coverage is limited.

3.label: Comprehensive
3.meaning: Comprehensive legal framework — privacy policy, ToS, cookie notice, GDPR compliance, accessibility.

1.label: Free
1.meaning: Free service — no payment or subscription signals detected. Ad-supported or grant-funded.

2.label: Pay-per-use
2.meaning: Pay-per-use model — transactional pricing, credit-based system, or usage-based billing.

3.label: Subscription
3.meaning: Subscription model — monthly or annual plans, recurring billing, SaaS pricing detected.

1.label: Unicast
1.meaning: Unicast delivery — single-origin direct connection, no CDN or proxy layer detected.

2.label: Multicast
2.meaning: Relay or proxy — traffic is routed through one or more intermediary network layers.

3.label: Anycast / Edge
3.meaning: Anycast or edge delivery — CDN with global points of presence, geometric routing to nearest edge.

1.label: Outbound
1.meaning: Outbound delivery — server pushes content to client, one-directional data flow.

2.label: Relay / Proxy
2.meaning: Relay or bidirectional — traffic passes through an intermediary or flows in both directions.

3.label: Inbound
3.meaning: Inbound data collection — client submits data to server as the primary mode of interaction.

1.label: Pull / Poll
1.meaning: Pull model — client must explicitly request updates, no server-initiated delivery mechanism.

2.label: Subscribe
2.meaning: Subscribe model — RSS, Atom feed, or webhook subscription mechanism detected.

3.label: Push
3.meaning: Push model — server initiates delivery via WebSocket, SSE, or mobile push notification.

1.label: Stateless
1.meaning: Stateless — no session cookies or persistent state detected. Each request is independent.

2.label: Short session
2.meaning: Short session — session cookie present, expires at browser close or within 24 hours.

3.label: Long-lived
3.meaning: Long-lived session — persistent cookie with expiry beyond 30 days. Extended tracking exposure.

1.label: Weak / None
1.meaning: Weak or no encryption — HTTP only or minimal security header coverage. High interception risk.

2.label: Basic TLS
2.meaning: Basic TLS — HTTPS present but security header suite is incomplete. Partial protection.

3.label: Hardened TLS
3.meaning: Hardened TLS — HTTPS with full security header suite: HSTS, CSP, XCTO, XFO all present.

1.label: Heavy
1.meaning: Heavy tracker presence — multiple tracking categories detected in the initial HTTP response.

2.label: Moderate
2.meaning: Moderate tracking — one or two tracker categories detected in the initial response.

3.label: Clean
3.meaning: Clean — no known tracker categories detected in the initial HTTP response at the network level.

1.label: None
1.meaning: No security audit evidence — no bug bounty program, penetration test, or certification signals.

2.label: Self-assessed
2.meaning: Self-assessed — bug bounty program or self-certification referenced on the site.

3.label: Third-party
3.meaning: Third-party audited — ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS, or equivalent independent certification.
